adverse_parent.finding: Over all 2^(n(n-1)/2) registries the direct optimizer signature is constant while terminal complexity spans 1..n, so completeness proved on a freely chosen registry does not transfer.

question: Does restricting to the source-complete quotient make production completeness identifiable, and if so does it also make the registry identifiable?

model_as_frozen.candidate_moves: all (source, target) with source > target — strictly resource-decreasing
model_as_frozen.terminal_complexity: max{ s : s has no outgoing edge in the registry }
model_as_frozen.direct_optimizer_signature: {feasible_state_count: n, optimum_value: 1, optimum_witness: 1} — constant by construction
model_as_frozen.source_complete: every state in 2..n has at least one outgoing edge in the registry

claims_to_test.statement: terminal_complexity(n, R) == 1 if and only if R is source-complete.
claims_to_test.kind: exact characterisation, proved and exhaustively checked

claims_to_test.statement: The number of source-complete registries on n states is the product over s in 2..n of (2^(s-1) - 1), and this equals the frozen R12 histogram's count at terminal complexity 1 for every n in 2..6.
claims_to_test.kind: closed form cross-checked against already-frozen evidence

claims_to_test.statement: The direct optimizer signature remains constant across the source-complete quotient, so the quotient does NOT make the registry identifiable.

why_C_matters: R12 conflated two failures: completeness was not identifiable, and the registry was not identifiable. If A and B hold while C also holds, the quotient repairs the first and leaves the second standing. Reporting only A and B would overstate the repair.

controls.statement: The recomputed count at terminal complexity 1 must equal the value already frozen in REGISTRY_NONIDENTIFIABILITY_R12_RESULTS.json for every n in 2..6. A mismatch means this packet has re-modelled the object rather than quotienting it, and is CANNOT_CHECK.

Claim A must be checked in BOTH directions over every registry: no source-complete registry with complexity != 1, and no non-source-complete registry with complexity == 1. Checking one direction would not distinguish an iff from an implication.
For every n >= 2 at least one registry must be non-source-complete with complexity > 1, otherwise the quotient is vacuous and separates nothing.
Claim C must be measured by collecting the signature over the source-complete subfamily and counting distinct values, not asserted from the constructor.

conditions: B matches the frozen histogram at every n
C holds: signature stays constant on the quotient
terminals.licenses: A bounded statement that completeness is identifiable and equal to 1 on the source-complete quotient, while registry identifiability is not repaired.
does_not_license: any change to the R12 record
any claim about registries outside this frozen finite model

conditions: C fails: the signature varies across the source-complete quotient
terminals.reading: Stronger than expected — the quotient would make the registry identifiable too.

conditions: A fails in either direction, or B does not match the frozen histogram
terminals.reading: Source-completeness is not the right quotient. Priority 6 is refuted as stated.
This packet is not measuring the frozen object. No claim is read either way.

falsifiability_self_check.note: The predicted outcome is deliberately the mixed one: it repairs the completeness half of the R12 negative and explicitly leaves the transfer half adverse.

stop_rule: Outcomes are read once. Whatever terminal is reached, the R12 record and its authority fields are not edited by this packet.
